Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions will be repeated during the Q&A portion of the call. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Investment Officer; and David Wong, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust market appreciation, record net inflows, and strategic acquisitions that expanded our capabilities in high-growth areas. Our AUM grew to $1.28 trillion.

Michael Chen: Thank you, John. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $4.62 billion, representing a 13% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, resilient fee rates in alternatives, and performance fee crystallization across our active strategies. Our expenses were $3.0 billion, resulting in net income of $1.3 billion. We continue to manage our expenses prudently, achieving an operating margin of 36.2%, up 420 basis points year-over-year.

As we unpack these results, let me start with our assets under management—or AUM—performance, which remains the cornerstone of our franchise. Our disciplined investment process, diversified product suite, and client-centric distribution strategy continue to drive resilient growth amid a dynamic macro environment. At quarter-end September 30, 2024, our total AUM stood at $1.28 trillion, up 6.2% quarter-over-quarter from $1.205 trillion at the end of Q2, and 14.8% year-over-year from $1.115 trillion in Q3 2023. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of positive organic growth, excluding market and FX impacts.

Breaking down the drivers, our QoQ AUM expansion was fueled by strong market appreciation of 4.1%, or $49 billion, net client inflows of $18 billion, and a modest foreign exchange tailwind of $6 billion, primarily from a weaker USD against the EUR and JPY. Year-over-year, market beta contributed 9.2%, with net flows adding another 4.1%, and FX providing the balance. Notably, our long-term net flows—over 3-, 5-, and 10-year periods—remain robust at $45 billion, $112 billion, and $285 billion, respectively, underscoring the stickiness of our institutional and HNW client base.

Turning to the asset class breakdown, which highlights our balanced positioning and ability to capture thematic flows: Equities at $576 billion, or 45% of total, grew 8.1% QoQ and 18.2% YoY, benefiting from the ongoing AI-driven rally, with the S&P 500 up about 22% YTD and MSCI World ex-US gaining 15%. We saw $12 billion in net inflows here, led by active large-cap growth strategies like our Apex Global Equity Partners fund, which outperformed its benchmark by 210 basis points in Q3. Retail channels, particularly via our low-cost ETFs such as the Apex U.S. Tech Innovators ETF mirroring the Nasdaq-100 but with ESG overlays, captured about 60% of these flows. Regionally, APAC ex-Japan contributed $4 billion, driven by sovereign wealth funds rotating into U.S. equities amid yen weakness.

Fixed Income at $384 billion, 30% of total, grew 2.9% QoQ and 8.7% YoY, reflecting the sector's sensitivity to the Fed's 50 basis points September cut and forward guidance for another 25 basis points in December. Our lift came from carry accrual and modest price appreciation in investment-grade corporates and EM bonds. Inflows totaled $5 billion, skewed toward short-duration and floating-rate products like our Apex Core Plus Bond Fund, which has seen AUM double YoY to $45 billion. Institutional clients in EMEA—pension funds like those akin to the UK's BT Pension Scheme—drove 40% of flows, hedging against sticky inflation. We continue to position for a steepener trade, with average portfolio duration at 5.2 years, up from 4.8 in Q2.

Alternatives at $192 billion, 15% of total, was the star performer with 9.4% QoQ growth and 22.5% YoY, outpacing the broader industry. Net inflows hit a record $9 billion, pushing AUM past $190 billion for the first time. Private equity and credit strategies, including our evergreen interval funds like Apex Direct Lending Partners yielding 10-12% net, attracted U.S. wirehouse flows and family offices seeking illiquidity premia amid compressed PE multiples. Our closed-end fund, Apex Infra Opportunities, launched in partnership with infrastructure plays, gathered $3.2 billion in its first full quarter. Latin America and Middle East sovereigns added $2.5 billion, capitalizing on energy transition themes.

Multi-asset at $77 billion, 6%, grew 4.2% QoQ and 11.3% YoY, buoyed by 401(k) glide path mandates and our robo-advisor platform, Apex WealthPath, which now serves 2.5 million users and drove $2 billion in flows via model delivery to RIAs. Cash and MMFs at $51 billion, 4%, dipped 1.2% QoQ but rose 5.6% YoY, with yield chase offset by rotations.

Strategically, we're leaning into digital transformation via the ApexOne platform—our Aladdin-like tech stack—which has reduced time-to-market for new ETFs to under 90 days, enabling rapid product iteration like our upcoming active fixed income ETF targeting 4-5% yields in a post-rate hike world. ESG integration across 70% of AUM has resonated, with our sustainable equity suite growing 25% YoY, aligning with EU SFDR regulations and CalPERS-style mandates. We're expanding in high-growth regions: APAC AUM now 18% of total, up from 14% YoY, fueled by a Singapore hub and tie-ups with local platforms.

This AUM growth directly translated to our revenue performance, a cornerstone of our business model where revenue is predominantly fee-based, with approximately 82% from management fees on average daily AUM, 11% from performance fees on alternatives and active equity, and the rest from distribution and admin services. Average AUM for the quarter was $1.24 trillion, up 11% YoY, driving fee revenue growth. Our blended annualized management fee rate held steady at 36.5 basis points, down just 10 bps sequentially due to mix shifts toward lower-fee ETFs, a trend we're managing through fee optimization.

AUM dynamics drove this uplift via three levers: market performance contributed $92 billion to ending AUM, or 72% of growth. Equities added $68 billion from a 7.2% rally driven by U.S. tech megacaps and European recovery, pushing equity average AUM up 16% YoY and contributing over 60% of fee growth there. Fixed income grew $18 billion on 2.5% appreciation amid falling yields, while alternatives saw $6 billion from J-curve unwind, with performance fees surging 28% YoY to $510 million from 15%+ NAV uplift in direct lending.

Net client flows delivered $48 billion in long-term inflows—our strongest since Q4 2021. Organic growth was $42 billion, with $32 billion into passive and smart-beta ETFs like our Apex Core S&P 500 ETF managing $145 billion and capturing 1.2% market share in U.S. large-cap ETFs. Active flows at $10 billion came from wirehouse channels like Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch, where ESG-integrated sleeves outperformed by 250 bps over three years. Retail net outflows of $2 billion were limited, offset by $5 billion in 401(k) rollovers. Inorganic flows from recent acquisitions added tailwind.

FX provided $4 billion, mainly from euro strength boosting our 28% EMEA book. Regionally, Americas grew average AUM 14% YoY on $35 billion inflows, driving 65% of fee revenue; EMEA up 9%, offset by UCITS ETFs; APAC fastest at 15% on $8 billion into Japan equity ETFs and private markets feeders.

We've launched technical initiatives like our AlignedFee platform on 40% of ETF AUM, recapturing 5-8 bps, and accelerating alternatives to 25% of AUM by 2026 via evergreen private credit funds with $15 billion commitments. Horizon AI Optimizer enhances alpha in quant equities.

Looking ahead, sustained AUM momentum with $150-180 billion projected net inflows from retirement flows and de-risking. Revenue elasticity to AUM is 1.1x.

Speaking of flows, total net flows came in at $18.4 billion for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. This marks our strongest quarterly net inflow since Q4 2021, driven by robust retail demand for our passive ETF suites amid the equity rally and institutional mandates in alternatives. Year-to-date through Q3, we've captured $42.7 billion in net flows, on track for our best year of organic growth since post-pandemic recovery.

Total inflows reached $52.3 billion, up 14% sequentially and 22% YoY. Outflows were $33.9 billion, a modest 5% QoQ increase but flat YoY, reflecting disciplined retention in active equities. Net-to-AUM ratio of 2.8%, above our 1.5% long-term average and competitive with BlackRock's 2.4% and Vanguard's 1.9%.

By channel: Long-term flows ex-money markets totaled $14.2 billion net, 77% of total. ETFs led with $11.6 billion, including $8.2 billion into Core Equity suite and $3.4 billion into Summit S&P 500 UCITS ETF benefiting from 5.7% Q3 S&P return. Active mutual funds added $2.8 billion in multi-asset like Target 2035 Retirement Fund. Money markets $4.2 billion net on 5.3% rates. Institutional $9.8 billion net, highlighted by $2.5 billion European pension into private credit; retail/advisor $8.6 billion, up 28% YoY via Wealthscape enhancements.

By asset class: Equities $9.7 billion net, passive +$10.4 billion offsetting active small-cap outflows. Fixed Income $4.1 billion, led by short-duration ESG bond ETFs. Alternatives standout $3.6 billion, including $1.8 billion into evergreen private markets interval funds, outpacing PIMCO. Multi-Asset $1.0 billion net.

Regionally: Americas $13.2 billion net, U.S. retail up 35% YoY on Model Marketplace with 1,200+ models. EMEA $3.7 billion on UCITS and MiFID II. APAC record $1.5 billion, up 52% YoY on Asia ex-Japan equities amid China stimulus and Nikkei rally.

Sequentially, flows accelerated from Q2's $12.1 billion, +41% YoY ahead of peer median. Redemption rates at 4.2% of AUM, down from 4.8%, with 92% one-year retention.

Initiatives: Product innovation with three active semi-liquid alts funds seeding $1.2 billion, attracting $800 million flows targeting $2 trillion interval market. AI-powered flow forecasting via Summit Analytics improved pipeline conversion 18%. Distribution added 450 RIAs to UMA platform.

Forward, $25-30 billion Q4 pipeline, 60% ETFs/alts. Risks from equity volatility, but diversified positioning and 15% high-margin alts provide resilience. Committed to 4-6% annual organic growth through 2026.

Our operating margin trends reflect robust operating leverage from AUM growth outpacing expenses. At 36.2%, up 420 bps YoY from 32.0% and 180 bps sequentially from Q1's 34.4%. On track for full-year 35-37%, ahead of prior 33-35% guide.

Revenue side: AUM up 14% YoY and 5% QoQ on 7% market tailwind in equities/fixed income. Average fees at 42 bps, modest 5 bps compression offset by 85 bps in alternatives on $180 billion AUM up 22% YoY, and 55 bps wealth fees.

Expenses rose 8% YoY to $1.45 billion below 10% guide, yielding 600 bps expansion. Comp/benefits up 9% to $750 million on merit pay, headcount +2% to 4,200. G&A flat via procurement and hybrid model.

Tech/data investments drove 300 bps improvement: $250 million roadmap, AI alpha generation across 40% of $400 billion systematic equity reducing research costs 15% via NLP on earnings/SEC filings. Robo-advisory Apex Digital Wealth to $50 billion AUM, acquisition costs down 20% to $450/account, 95% retention.

Regionally: Americas 39% margins up 500 bps on $720 billion AUM, DCIO flows. Europe 32% despite MiFID II, anchored by €120 billion SFDR strategies. APAC 34% on 25% AUM growth to $210 billion via China tie-ups.

'Scale, Simplify, Sustain' framework counters fee compression via alts to 20% AUM by 2025, ESG at 35%, blockchain custody. Targeting 2% annual margin creep. Risks from rate cuts, regs, but 45% recurring revenue and $4 billion cash buffer position well.

Before segment results, a few minutes on mergers and acquisitions, a key driver of inorganic growth. In asset management, with organic flows moderated by fee compression and passive shift, M&A scales AUM, diversifies, captures alpha in alts and sustainable investing. Disciplined bolt-ons: accretive, aligned, leveraging global platform over 50 countries, wirehouses like Morgan Stanley, Merrill Lynch.

Headline: Q3 closed two deals adding $28 billion AUM, YTD $52 billion or 14% of $372 billion ending—wait, scaling to our total, these bolstered our trajectory to $1.28 trillion. Funded by cash from 92% FCF conversion and $1.2 billion term debt at 4.1% post-Fed cuts. Expect $185 million annualized revenue, $42 million first-year synergies from ops and cross-selling.

First, Horizon Sustainable Partners, London boutique in Article 9 SFDR ESG, $14 billion AUM in UCITS climate funds at 65 bps fees above our 42 bps blended. Closed Sept 15 post FCA/CBI approvals, YTD €1.2 billion inflows from Nordic/Benelux pensions on SFDR enhancements. Bolsters ESG to $48 billion, up 22% YoY; launching Q1 2025 active ETFs: net-zero equity index, ESG-private credit. Early RIA interest in US, ESG flows +15% QoQ per Morningstar.

Europe hotspot with MiFID III; Horizon integration: 80% systems to ApexOne OMS in 45 days, $18 million synergies. European AUM $92 billion, 25% total, fees to 48 bps.

Second, merger with Ventura Alternatives, San Francisco $14 billion evergreen privates: $9 billion PE feeders, $5 billion real assets data centers/renewables. Issued 12 million shares $2.1 billion, assumed/refinanced $450 million debt at SOFR+175 bps. Accretive 8% EPS year one, 15% year three, $24 million synergies from GP/co-invests.

Ventura aligns with privates tailwinds: $13 trillion global alts per Preqin, evergreens +28% YoY. Flagship Core PE 17% net IRR complements our $65 billion alts to $79 billion. Cross-placed $1.2 billion to institutional, CalPERS-like endowments targeting 10-12%. Accelerating Apex AI Sentinel ML for stress testing, -22% drawdowns.

US RIA alts allocation to 18% per Cerulli. Ventura's 45 pros join 1,200, retention bonuses. Harmonizing fees 1.2%/0.9%, co-branded interval fund targeting $5 billion by 2025-end.

Pipeline $75 billion across 15: prioritizing APAC 12% CAGR per McKinsey, LOIs Singapore quant hedge $8 billion Asia L/S 1.4%+18% carry, diligence Tokyo RE amid J-REIT compression. Minority stakes with calls.

Framework: capability adjacency—94% deals in alts/ESG/quant; distribution leverage—25-30% AUM growth post-close; tech/ops 20-25% savings via cloud/blockchain NAV, -60% recon times.

Risks: execution/retention ring-fenced $150 million incentives, 92% retention. Reg scrutiny post-Franklin/Legg, clean track. Volatility from elections/inflation, but 70% pipeline 8-10x FRE vs 12x industry.

These underscore inorganic growth, fee resilience, mid-teens EPS. $3.2 billion dry powder, net debt/EBITDA 1.4x for 2025.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by positioning for further Fed easing while emphasizing illiquidity premia in private markets and ESG themes resilient to volatility. We launched a new evergreen private credit fund this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $3.2 billion in commitments already, enhancing our alternatives platform.

David Wong: Thank you, Lisa. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by record $1.5 billion net flows there, up 52% year-over-year, driven by partnerships in Hong Kong and Singapore and launches of Asia ex-Japan equity products.

John Reynolds: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes sustaining organic growth through product innovation, deepening tech integration for efficiency, and pursuing disciplined M&A to build scale in alternatives and ESG.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one one. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Goldman Sachs.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the recent mergers and acquisitions activity and how they factor into your growth outlook?

John Reynolds: Thanks, Emily. As Michael detailed, the Horizon and Ventura deals added meaningful scale immediately accretive, with strong synergies already materializing. Horizon bolsters our ESG leadership in Europe, while Ventura supercharges privates, cross-selling into our channels. Pipeline remains robust, focused on APAC adjacency. This supports mid-teens EPS growth, with dry powder for more.

Emily Carter: Thank you. And a follow-up on the net flows outlook into Q4 and beyond?

Michael Chen: Emily, our $25-30 billion Q4 pipeline is solid, 60% ETFs and alts, backed by Fed easing and election clarity. Long-term, 4-6% organic AUM growth through 2026 via innovation like semi-liquid alts and AI distribution tools. Retention at 92% gives confidence despite volatility risks.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Harris with JPMorgan.

Tom Harris: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of your alternatives funds?

Lisa Patel: Sure, Tom. Alternatives shone with $3.6 billion net flows and 9.4% AUM growth. Flagships like Direct Lending Partners at 10-12% yields drew institutions seeking premium amid high rates. Ventura integration adds 17% IRR PE expertise, with AI Sentinel enhancing risk models—backtests show 22% drawdown reduction. Outpacing peers, now 15% of AUM targeting 20%.

Tom Harris: And how is the new evergreen private credit product performing relative to expectations?

David Wong: Exceeding, Tom. $3.2 billion gathered first quarter via wirehouses and RIAs, tapping 18% model portfolio allocations. Early sovereign commitments position for $15 billion scale, mirroring Blackstone BCRED success, with strong pipeline from family offices de-risking into illiquids.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to John Reynolds for closing remarks.

John Reynolds: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
